title: The Fed traces how an investment setback could reach lenders through leases, collateral and funding
bank: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
summary: A setback in data-centre investment could reach lenders through leases and guarantees before a large technology company misses a bond payment. The Federal Reserve Board’s November 13 assessment places that exposure in a system with expensive assets and notable leverage among financial intermediaries. It judges vulnerabilities from business and household debt and from funding moderate overall. Its evidence generally runs through October 28, but the most comprehensive hedge-fund positions were six months older. The report identifies which balance sheets could transmit stress and what cushions they had when measured.

Higher expected earnings brought down the forward equity price-to-earnings ratio, which remained well above its historical median. The difference between the expected earnings yield and the real ten-year Treasury yield was near the low end of its historical range. Treasury yields rose, with the estimated term premium above its historical median. The price response to an order imbalance was above its post-2014 median in the two-year note and near its median at ten years. Corporate bonds still traded with tight bid-ask spreads. High-yield credit spreads widened moderately but remained below their long-run median. The first spread measures trading costs, the second the extra yield investors demand for holding corporate debt.

Combined business and household credit reached $45.3 trillion in the second quarter, up 4.6% in a year against nominal GDP growth of 6.6%. Business debt relative to GDP remained in its historical upper quartile. Investment-grade firms generally covered interest comfortably, while some private and lower-rated borrowers struggled. Adding unpaid interest to principal can mask a cash shortfall. Household debt relative to GDP was below its historical median and most homeowners had considerable equity. FHA mortgage delinquencies were rising and auto delinquency was well above its historical median. In commercial property, extensions limited forced sales even as refinancing remained difficult.

Box 2.2 records over $680 billion of advanced-computing debt issuance by October 2026, against $130 billion in all of 2023. Related public debt outstanding exceeded $1.1 trillion. Some private deals escape the issuance measure. Large cloud companies initially financed much investment internally. A developer can now borrow against a long lease from a highly rated tenant, while an equipment supplier’s residual-value guarantee can support the collateral. Among seven technology firms, undiscounted payments on leases awaiting commencement exceeded $1 trillion. Other obligations, including minimum-purchase contracts and residual-value guarantees, exceeded $2 trillion. Timing, conditions and valuation differ from the carrying value of debt, so adding the three figures would misstate immediate liabilities.

Those contracts can transfer losses back to stronger firms. High-yield funds, life insurers, business development companies and other private lenders also hold riskier subordinated positions in project vehicles. The largest US bank holding companies have close to $1 trillion of exposure across technology firms, developers, related financing vehicles and utilities. That broad exposure is covered by supervisory stress testing. A separate measure, bank credit commitments to other financial institutions, exceeded $2.8 trillion in the second quarter, roughly a quarter in private equity, business development companies and private credit combined. Commitments measure potential funding calls. A change in recorded private credit also warrants checking which existing loans the new Financial Accounts categories reclassified.

Hedge funds’ gross notional exposure relative to net assets reached a series high in the first quarter, concentrated at larger funds and spread across strategies even as Treasury cash-futures basis trading declined. Dealers subsequently reported little change in client leverage. Banks reported high regulatory capital, but their securities portfolios’ fair value was roughly $330 billion below book in the second quarter. A sale can realise a loss while a repo can raise cash against the same security for as long as the lender rolls the financing. Leverage at large life insurers remained high, while broker-dealers carried relatively low leverage and expanded intermediation.

About $28.2 trillion of money-like liabilities were potentially subject to withdrawal or rollover, equivalent to 87% of GDP. Banks relied less on uninsured deposits than at the 2022 peak. Government money funds, historically less exposed to large redemptions, accounted for most cash-management asset growth. Withdrawal requests at some nontraded business development companies eased, with limits still in place and net flows negative. Among 23 market contacts surveyed in September and October, 87% cited AI-related risks over the next 12–18 months. They saw cyberattack and fiscal sustainability as having the most severe potential consequences. How many people mention a risk and how damaging they think it could be answer different questions.

questions.question: Who would need cash first if data-centre occupancy or equipment resale values fell?
questions.detail: Map a representative project from its senior and subordinated financing through the developer, anchor tenant and equipment guarantor. Separate mandatory lease payments from contingent guarantees and record both their triggers and due dates. Compare the stressed cash flows with liquid resources at each entity. The undiscounted gross commitments in Box 2.2 can locate exposures but cannot be entered as a single immediate loss.

questions.question: Would a Treasury sell-off produce fund deleveraging, a bank capital loss, or both?
questions.detail: For funds, align changes in financing haircuts, margin requirements and positions by strategy. For banks, distinguish securities sold at a loss from pledged holdings and monitor dependence on rolling repo. Compare these indicators with price impact at two and ten years. Use the dates of the underlying fund filings and securities data, since the November publication does not make each observation current in October.

questions.question: Is deteriorating credit quality concentrated among borrowers whose payments reset soon?
questions.detail: Separate floating-rate and near-maturity borrowers from investment-grade issuers with fixed debt. Within the weaker group, compare cash interest coverage, interest added to principal, distressed exchanges and cash defaults. Check whether the new Financial Accounts classification changes the denominator. Distinguish new extensions from use of existing lines before inferring a contraction in the supply of credit.

questions.question: Which vehicles could meet withdrawals only by transferring liquidity pressure elsewhere?
questions.detail: Track redemption requests, limits, realised sales and new inflows separately for nontraded private-credit funds. Compare these with outflows from daily-dealing bond funds and the availability of bank credit lines. A fall in paid redemptions is less reassuring when unfulfilled requests rise. The contact survey can guide scenario selection, but loss estimates require portfolio quantities, funding terms and transaction prices.

limitation: The data have different observation dates. The Board’s market-contact survey measures concerns among respondents. The report supplies neither probabilities of those scenarios nor estimates of bank losses attributable to AI.
